appeal.letter:
Subject: Appeal Against Denial of Claim d16c167f-1b87-ef6b-69a1-a1cbe0b2a03e – Request for Re‑processing and Payment  

Claim Details  
Claim ID: d16c167f-1b87-ef6b-69a1-a1cbe0b2a03e  
Patient ID: d16c167f-1b87-ef6b-b3a0-d0c591c19404  
Patient Name: Bryon Herb Bernhard  
Date of Service: 2024‑04‑10  
Policy: Suraksha Silver Individual Health Plan (Plan Code SGH‑SILVER) – Coverage effective 2024‑01‑23  
Diagnosis: Osteoarthritis of knee (onset 2024‑04‑10)  
Procedure: Wheelchair accessory  
Claimed Amount: INR 300.00  

Grounds for Appeal – Condition Not Pre‑Existing  
The policy definition states that any condition first diagnosed on or after the policy start date is NOT a Pre‑Existing Disease, regardless of chronicity [suraksha_silver_policy#5]. Osteoarthritis of the knee for the patient was first diagnosed on 2024‑04‑10, which is after the policy start date of 2024‑01‑23; therefore the condition does not meet the definition of a Pre‑Existing Disease.  

Grounds for Appeal – Waiting Period Inapplicable  
Clause 4.2 provides a waiting period only for expenses related to a Pre‑Existing Disease as defined in Clause 2.2. Since the diagnosis does not satisfy the definition, the 36‑month waiting period does not apply to this claim [suraksha_silver_policy#11].  

Burden of Proof  
According to the insurer’s own claims procedure, the burden of proving that an exclusion or waiting period applies rests with the insurer, which must produce documentary evidence of a diagnosis or treatment prior to the policy start date [claims_procedure_and_grievance#6]. No such evidence has been furnished, rendering the denial unsupported.  

Clinical Necessity  
The wheelchair accessory is required for safe mobility and effective management of the patient’s knee osteoarthritis and therefore qualifies as medically necessary treatment under the policy definition of Medically Necessary care [suraksha_silver_policy#4]. The treating physician will attach detailed clinical notes confirming this necessity.  

Reference to Denial Standards  
The insurer’s denial fails to comply with the standards set out in the policy and the claims procedure, which require proof of a pre‑existing condition before applying the waiting period and obligate the insurer to bear the burden of that proof [claims_procedure_and_grievance#6][suraksha_silver_policy#5]. The denial therefore contravenes these stipulated requirements.  

Specific Request  
In view of the foregoing, we respectfully request that Claim ID d16c167f-1b87-ef6b-69a1-a1cbe0b2a03e be re‑processed and the amount of INR 300.00 be paid in full, as the waiting period exclusion is inapplicable [suraksha_silver_policy#11].  

Insurance Desk (on behalf of the treating provider)

citations.quote:
### 2.2 Pre-Existing Disease (PED)
Pre-Existing Disease means any condition, ailment, injury or disease that was diagnosed by a physician, or for which medical advice or treatment was received, within 48 months PRIOR TO the first policy start date. A condition that is first diagnosed ON OR AFTER the policy start date is NOT a Pre-Existing Disease, irrespective of whether the condition is chronic i

citations.section: Suraksha Silver Individual Health Plan (Policy Wording) > 4. Waiting Periods > 4.2 Pre-Existing Disease Waiting Period
citations.quote:
### 4.2 Pre-Existing Disease Waiting Period
Expenses related to a Pre-Existing Disease (as defined in Clause 2.2) are covered only after 36 months of continuous coverage from the first policy start date. This waiting period applies ONLY to conditions meeting the definition in Clause 2.2.

citations.section: Claims Procedure, Denial Standards and Grievance Redressal > C3. Standards for Denial > C3.2 Burden of Proof for Exclusions and Waiting Periods
citations.quote:
### C3.2 Burden of Proof for Exclusions and Waiting Periods
The insurer bears the burden of proving that an exclusion or waiting period applies. For a Pre-Existing Disease denial, the insurer must show documentary evidence that the condition was diagnosed or treated before the policy start date.

citations.section: Suraksha Silver Individual Health Plan (Policy Wording) > 2. Definitions > 2.1 Medically Necessary
citations.quote:
## 2. Definitions  
### 2.1 Medically Necessary
Treatment that is required for the medical management of the illness or injury suffered by the insured; must not exceed the level of care necessary to provide safe, adequate and appropriate medical care; and must be prescribed by a medical practitioner in line with generally accepted standards of practice.
